title: Intrinsically disordered proteins with Professor Priyanka Joshi, Ph.D.
summary: Parag interviews Professor Priyanka Joshi about her work on intrinsically disordered proteins and developing new ways to study and drug them.
body_markdown:
Unlike “globular” proteins that adopt stable structures that are relatively easy to analyze,[intrinsically disordered proteins](https://www.nautilus.bio/blog/advancing-the-identification-of-biomarkers-and-drug-targets-as-part-of-the-arpa-h-funded-seeds-consortium/) adopt many context-dependent shapes. These shapes may drive diverse functions, but they are also difficult to capture and study. This represents a large gap in our understanding of biology, given that most proteins may have intrinsically disordered regions. Thankfully, researchers like Professor[Priyanka Joshi, Ph.D.](https://www.joshilab.org/priyanka-joshi) , from Georgetown University have devoted themselves to studying intrinsically disordered proteins and are developing new approaches and leveraging new technologies like the Nautilus Voyager™ Platform to discover how their dynamic structures influence biological function. Because intrinsically disordered proteins often aggregate in disease, this work is not only essential to our understanding of biology but may also enable the development of effective biomarkers and treatments for diseases like Alzheimer’s.


Parag interviews Professor Joshi on this episode of Translating Proteomics to discover:


- What intrinsically disordered proteins are.
- How intrinsically disordered proteins influence biology and why they’re hard to study.
- How the recently announced[SEEDS Consortium](https://www.georgetown.edu/news/georgetown-and-buck-institute-awarded-up-to-51-7m-to-predict-protein-changes-linked-to-alzheimers-and-some-cancers/) is studying intrinsically disordered proteins.


Stream the episode on[YouTube](https://youtu.be/BPNiCxHl5tA) ,[Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/0p8hgFFOaw1d4ZrAOKyl7T?si=JPj4-ssnRsuGQRVWWVuawA&utm_source=copy-link) , or[Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/intrinsically-disordered-proteins-with-professor/id1739213971?i=1000798597073) .


### Chapters:


**00:00** – Introduction to Prof. Priyanka Joshi, Ph.D.
**04:35** – What are intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs)?
**11:41** – When do intrinsically disordered proteins go bad in disease?
**23:02** – Archetypal Intrinsically disordered proteins – c-Myc/Max, p53, and Tau
**38:26** – Barriers to solving the problems associated with intrinsically disordered proteins
**43:30** – The future of intrinsically disordered protein research and introducing the SEEDS Consortium
